questions.stem: The heart on the right shows a thickened ventricular wall with a smaller chamber cavity compared with the normal heart on the left. This geometry most directly predisposes to which functional type of heart failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

explanation.summary: A concentrically hypertrophied, stiff, small-cavity ventricle fills poorly during diastole while contractility is preserved, producing HFpEF (diastolic dysfunction).
explanation.whyCorrect: A concentrically hypertrophied, stiff, small-cavity ventricle fills poorly during diastole while contractility is preserved, producing HFpEF (diastolic dysfunction).

questions.stem: The point marked as ventricular dysfunction on this curve sits on the flattened, descending portion. For a dilated failing ventricle operating there, what happens to stroke volume when end-diastolic volume is increased further?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stroke volume rises in direct proportion to volume

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stroke volume rises little or actually falls

explanation.summary: On the descending/flattened limb of the Frank-Starling relationship, sarcomeres are already overstretched, so added volume yields little or no gain in stroke volume and can worsen output.
explanation.whyCorrect: On the descending/flattened limb of the Frank-Starling relationship, sarcomeres are already overstretched, so added volume yields little or no gain in stroke volume and can worsen output.

questions.stem: A clinician presses on the swollen lower legs shown and the skin retains a lasting indentation. This physical finding is most characteristically associated with which category of disease?

explanation.summary: The lasting indentation identifies pitting edema, which reflects excess mobile interstitial fluid and is classically linked to cardiac, hepatic, or renal disease. Myxedema is nonpitting, angioedema and cellulitis are localized and acute, and lymphatic obstruction tends to produce nonpitting lymphedema.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lasting indentation identifies pitting edema, which reflects excess mobile interstitial fluid and is classically linked to cardiac, hepatic, or renal disease. Myxedema is nonpitting, angioedema and cellulitis are localized and acute, and lymphatic obstruction tends to produce nonpitting lymphedema.

questions.stem: The far-right branch of this classification of edema causes points to a protein-losing renal process. Which single laboratory abnormality would you most expect to underlie that branch?

explanation.summary: The protein-loss branch reflects nephrotic-range urinary albumin loss, which lowers serum albumin and thus plasma oncotic pressure, promoting fluid movement into the interstitium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The protein-loss branch reflects nephrotic-range urinary albumin loss, which lowers serum albumin and thus plasma oncotic pressure, promoting fluid movement into the interstitium.

questions.stem: In the capillary force diagram shown, which change to the depicted forces would MOST directly favor net filtration and lead to edema?

explanation.summary: A rise in capillary hydrostatic pressure pushes more fluid out of the capillary into the interstitium. Raising plasma oncotic pressure or albumin would pull fluid back in, reduced permeability limits leak, and higher interstitial hydrostatic pressure opposes filtration.
explanation.whyCorrect: A rise in capillary hydrostatic pressure pushes more fluid out of the capillary into the interstitium. Raising plasma oncotic pressure or albumin would pull fluid back in, reduced permeability limits leak, and higher interstitial hydrostatic pressure opposes filtration.

questions.stem: The green vessels emphasized in this illustration perform which function that is critical to preventing edema?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delivering oxygenated blood to the tissues

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exchanging gases across the capillary bed

explanation.summary: The green channels are lymphatic vessels, which collect the roughly 20 L/day of interstitial fluid not reabsorbed by venules and return it to the veins. Impairment of this drainage causes lymphedema.
explanation.whyCorrect: The green channels are lymphatic vessels, which collect the roughly 20 L/day of interstitial fluid not reabsorbed by venules and return it to the veins. Impairment of this drainage causes lymphedema.

questions.stem: In this summary diagram, the inflow branch grouping malabsorption, nephrotic syndrome, liver failure, and malnutrition acts through a fall in plasma oncotic pressure. Which underlying change best accounts for that branch?

explanation.summary: Albumin is the principal determinant of plasma oncotic pressure. Loss (nephrotic syndrome), decreased synthesis (liver failure, malnutrition), or poor intake/absorption lowers albumin, reducing the inward oncotic force and allowing fluid to accumulate in the interstitium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Albumin is the principal determinant of plasma oncotic pressure. Loss (nephrotic syndrome), decreased synthesis (liver failure, malnutrition), or poor intake/absorption lowers albumin, reducing the inward oncotic force and allowing fluid to accumulate in the interstitium.

questions.stem: The ECG tracing shown, paired with the depicted myocardial change, meets diagnostic voltage criteria. What anatomic abnormality produces the high-amplitude QRS complexes in the lateral leads?

choices.label: C
choices.text: A left bundle branch conduction delay

explanation.summary: The diagram shows a thickened left ventricle and the ECG shows tall QRS complexes. Increased LV mass generates a larger electrical signal, producing high-voltage QRS complexes in the lateral leads that meet voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy, often with a lateral strain pattern.
explanation.whyCorrect: The diagram shows a thickened left ventricle and the ECG shows tall QRS complexes. Increased LV mass generates a larger electrical signal, producing high-voltage QRS complexes in the lateral leads that meet voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy, often with a lateral strain pattern.

questions.stem: This chest radiograph is from a patient with left heart failure following a myocardial infarction. What do the fluffy, symmetric perihilar opacities most likely represent?

choices.label: D
choices.text: A wedge-shaped infarct from pulmonary embolism

explanation.summary: Left ventricular failure raises pulmonary venous and capillary pressure, forcing fluid into the interstitium and alveoli. On chest X-ray this appears as symmetric perihilar (bat-wing) opacities with vascular redistribution, characteristic of cardiogenic pulmonary edema rather than the focal consolidation of pneumonia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Left ventricular failure raises pulmonary venous and capillary pressure, forcing fluid into the interstitium and alveoli. On chest X-ray this appears as symmetric perihilar (bat-wing) opacities with vascular redistribution, characteristic of cardiogenic pulmonary edema rather than the focal consolidation of pneumonia.

questions.stem: This illustration depicts the constellation of findings caused by a specific cardiac syndrome. Which underlying hemodynamic disturbance most directly produces the pulmonary congestion shown?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tricuspid regurgitation raising right atrial pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduced pulmonary arterial pressure from hypovolemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevated systemic venous pressure from right ventricular failure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Elevated left atrial and pulmonary venous pressure

explanation.summary: The depicted findings (orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, tachycardia, pulmonary congestion) are those of left-sided heart failure. When the left ventricle cannot eject or fill effectively, blood backs up into the left atrium and pulmonary veins, raising hydrostatic pressure and driving fluid into the alveoli, producing pulmonary congestion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The depicted findings (orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, tachycardia, pulmonary congestion) are those of left-sided heart failure. When the left ventricle cannot eject or fill effectively, blood backs up into the left atrium and pulmonary veins, raising hydrostatic pressure and driving fluid into the alveoli, producing pulmonary congestion.

questions.stem: This stepwise algorithm for managing chronic systolic heart failure separates the numbered core therapies from a side branch (loop diuretics). What best explains why the loop diuretic branch is set apart?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loop diuretics are the mandatory first step before any other agent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loop diuretics replace the need for an MRA in every patient

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loop diuretics are used only in preserved-EF (diastolic) heart failure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loop diuretics relieve congestive symptoms but do not reduce mortality

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loop diuretics reduce cardiac remodeling and improve survival

explanation.summary: The numbered core agents (ACEi/ARB or ARNI plus beta-blocker, then SGLT2 inhibitor, then MRA) are shown driving the mortality and morbidity benefit. Loop diuretics are added at any step based on signs and symptoms of congestion; they are for symptom control and do not reduce mortality.
explanation.whyCorrect: The numbered core agents (ACEi/ARB or ARNI plus beta-blocker, then SGLT2 inhibitor, then MRA) are shown driving the mortality and morbidity benefit. Loop diuretics are added at any step based on signs and symptoms of congestion; they are for symptom control and do not reduce mortality.

questions.stem: This schematic shows a drug inhibiting a membrane pump in the cardiac myocyte, altering ion gradients. What is the ultimate cardiac effect produced by this mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coronary vasodilation with increased oxygen supply

choices.label: B
choices.text: Slowing of AV nodal conduction only

explanation.summary: Digoxin inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular sodium. This reduces the driving force of the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger, so less calcium is extruded and intracellular calcium rises, increasing the force of contraction. Digoxin improves symptoms but does not improve mortality.
explanation.whyCorrect: Digoxin inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular sodium. This reduces the driving force of the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger, so less calcium is extruded and intracellular calcium rises, increasing the force of contraction. Digoxin improves symptoms but does not improve mortality.
